body.question: Someone loses their job, searches for months, then stops looking. In many official unemployment statistics, are they counted as unemployed?
options: Yes, they still have no job
No, they are no longer counted
body.reveal: In many countries only those with no work who are actively looking are counted. The ILO counts as unemployed those not working but willing, available and having actively searched for work. Broader US measures such as U-4 add discouraged workers, who stopped looking.

probes.question: To be counted as unemployed under the ILO definition, a person must have done what?
True or false: the unemployment rate is the number of unemployed people as a percentage of the labour force.

claims.claim: In many countries only those with no work who are actively looking are counted as unemployed
claims.quote: In many countries, only those who have no work but are actively looking for work or qualifying for social security benefits are counted as unemployed.
claims.note: Card omits 'or qualifying for social security benefits'; consider 'only those with no work who are actively looking (or qualifying for benefits)'.

claims.claim: Someone who stopped looking is no longer counted as unemployed in many official statistics (question answer)
claims.quote: Those who have given up looking for work and sometimes those who are on government "retraining" programs are not officially counted among the unemployed

claims.claim: ILO counts as unemployed those not working but willing, available and having actively searched for work (probe p1)
claims.quote: those who are currently not working but are willing and able to work for pay, currently available to work, and have actively searched for work

claims.claim: Broader US measures such as U-4 add discouraged workers, who stopped looking
claims.quote: those who have stopped looking for work because current economic conditions make them believe that no work is available for them
claims.note: Page lists U-4 as U-3 plus discouraged workers in its US Bureau of Labor Statistics section.

claims.claim: Unemployment rate is the number of unemployed as a percentage of the labour force (probe p2)
claims.quote: Unemployment is measured by the unemployment rate, which is the number of people who are unemployed as a percentage of the labour force
